subject: SummitPay — SSO guardrails, SCIM mappings & service-account runbook
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Megan Liu <megan.liu@summitpay.com>, Sujal Patel <sujal@summitpay.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: SummitPay — SSO guardrails, SCIM mappings & service-account runbook

Hi Megan / Sujal —

Great to meet last week. Per our discussion, I pulled together a concise plan to align Redwood + SummitPay on access controls for production onboarding. High-level agenda and asks below. I’ve attached an attribute mapping CSV and a first-pass runbook draft.

Agenda / scope
- SSO / SAML assertion mapping (NameID, email, groups, role claims)
- SCIM provisioning scope and delta (create/update/deprovision semantics)
- IP allowlist (egress NAT & customer inbound ranges)
- Service-account patterns (who creates keys, rotation, ephemeral vs long-lived)
- Org policies & RBAC mapping (groups → Redwood roles)
- Cutover window, canary plan, rollback criteria

Asks for your team before our technical sync:
1) Confirm the SCIM attribute that SummitPay currently uses for canonical user ID (email vs employee_id). I attached summitpay-sso-attribute-mapping.csv — please populate the right column where values differ.
2) Provide your production outbound IP ranges we should whitelist for webhook callbacks and admin UI (or confirm you prefer CIDR allowlist).
3) Any policy constraints around service accounts (e.g., SOC2 requirements that only SRE can store keys) or internal policy that would prevent us from creating managed service accounts on your tenant.
4) Preferred cutover window (we suggested Oct 12 02:00–04:00 UTC below; open to adjustments).

Next steps: once you confirm the three items above we’ll schedule a 45-min technical run-through with Jonas (engineering) and Neha (security lead) to finalize the runbook and test plan.

Attachments: summitpay-sso-attribute-mapping.csv (please edit), runbook-draft-v1.pdf, svc-account-guidelines.md

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Kimberly Park
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Redwood Inference — Production-first inference for ML teams

From: Megan Liu <megan.liu@summitpay.com>

Cc: 
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SummitPay — SSO guardrails, SCIM mappings & service-account runbook

Thanks Kim — this looks good and very clear. Quick answers and a couple clarifying questions from our side: 

1) SCIM canonical ID: we currently use employee_id for provisioning (not email). I updated the mapping CSV and re-attached.
2) IP allowlist: our security team requires both per-service CIDR and ephemeral NAT egress ranges for the app. I can export the list — will send by eod tomorrow.
3) Service accounts: policy is that only our infra team can hold long-lived keys; however we allow provider-managed ephemeral accounts for integrations if keys expire within 7 days and are rotated automatically. Is Redwood able to support ephemeral service accounts with short TTLs and automated rotation?
4) Cutover window: Oct 12 02:00–04:00 UTC works for us for a canary, provided the rollback is automated.

Also, for SCIM, will Redwood support filtering on group membership so we can restrict certain internal groups from being provisioned?

I’ll loop in our infra lead Sujal for the IP list and infra policy.

Best,
Megan Liu
Security Engineer, SummitPay
megan.liu@summitpay.com

Folks — forwarding Megan’s reply and the updated mapping. Key asks we need to own:

- Confirm SCIM canonical ID handling (SummitPay uses employee_id) — Jonas, can you validate our SCIM connector handles employee_id as externalId and propose the mapping change?
- Service accounts: SummitPay wants ephemeral provider-managed service accounts with TTL <= 7 days. Neha, do we have an approved pattern for ephemeral service-account rotation that satisfies SOC2 controls? If not, list the gaps and mitigation.
- IP allowlist: Sujal will send both service CIDRs and egress NAT ranges. Monica, please prepare the admin UI whitelist page and ensure webhook retry/backoff is configured for transient blockages.

Proposed timeline:
- Today EOD: internal owners confirm gaps and owners (Jonas/Neha/Monica).
- Thu 10/07: 45-min tech run-through with SummitPay (Jonas + Neha present).
- Tue 10/12 02:00–04:00 UTC: canary cutover in production (one cluster, 10% traffic).

Attachments: summitpay-sso-attribute-mapping.csv (updated by customer), runbook-draft-v1.pdf (internal draft).

Please reply with short bullets (I’ll consolidate and send to SummitPay).

Thanks — Kim

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Oct 2027 14:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: SummitPay — SSO guardrails, SCIM mappings & service-account runbook

Kimberly — thanks for the forward and clear asks. Short bullets from engineering/security side: 

- SCIM: we support using employee_id as externalId. I reviewed the updated CSV; mapping looks good. We’ll add a translation layer in the connector so email remains a visible attribute but employee_id is the authoritative externalId. Target: PR for connector + unit tests by Thu 10/07 EOD.

- Service accounts: we can support ephemeral provider-managed service accounts with automatic key rotation and 72-hour TTL out of the box. The current rotation system integrates with our KMS and issues short-lived certificates that the customer can bind to their SSO session. For SOC2 controls requiring restricted access to long-lived secrets, the recommended pattern is: Redwood creates ephemeral identities scoped to the integration, keys rotate automatically, and auditing is forwarded to customer SIEM via syslog. I attached svc-account-guidelines.md with details.

- Group filtering: we can accept a SCIM filter attribute (e.g., exclude groups with prefix internal_) — will expose a config flag in the tenant settings.

- IP allowlist: support for both static CIDR and published NAT egress ranges — will provide the published egress list (ipv4/ipv6) and a webhook backoff/retry plan.

- Runbook & rollback: propose an automated rollback that disables SCIM provisioning and flips the traffic routing to the previous model if error rate > 1% or user provisioning failures > 0.5% for 10 minutes.

Next steps:
1) I’ll open a connector PR and the runbook change by Thu 10/07.
2) Neha — please confirm audit/export fields required by security; I can add hooks.
3) Kim — confirm meeting with SummitPay for Thu 10/07 11:00 AM PT / 18:00 UTC.

If all good I’ll attach the PR and the test checklist to the drive folder.

Jonas Weber
Senior Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
